newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel to meet on Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel to meet on Gingrich.

text.p: The House ethics committee will meet January 8 to begin the final phase of its investigation of House Speaker Newt Gingrich -- one day after Gingrich offers himself for re-election as speaker, the committee said on Tuesday.

A committee announcement said it would meet to receive the findings of an investigative subcommittee that found Gingrich had violated House rules by using funds of tax-free foundations for political purposes.
The decision meant House Republicans would likely be asked to vote for Gingrich without knowing what punishment the committee will recommend.

Gingrich admitted violating House ethics rules, providing inaccurate information to investigators and failing to ensure that a college course he taught complied with laws barring use of tax-exempt organisations for partisan political purposes.

The ethics committee said it will meet in closed session to receive the findings of the four-member panel that has been investigating charges against Gingrich and vote on accepting Gingrich's waiver of a "trial" by the full committee.

It said there would then be a meeting in open session to receive submissions by special counsel James Cole and a counsel for Gingrich on the question of punishment. Republican leaders said they believed the puniushment would be a mild one that would not affect Gingrich's position as speaker.
